q8.answer: Session state lives in one shared Redis instance, in a hash keyed sess:{sha256(session id)}. Either app instance hashes the ID from the cookie and runs the CHECK script against Redis, so no state is held in an instance.

q9.answer: Failures are kept in Redis in the sorted set lf:{sha256(email)}, one entry per attempt (member = random nonce, score = Redis time in ms). The GATE script drops entries whose score is older than 10 minutes before counting.

q10.answer: CHECK compares the Redis clock (now) to the record's abs_expires_at, and the key's existence covers the 30-minute idle limit. If valid, it resets the TTL to min(1800 s, abs_expires_at - now) and returns the user_id.

q11.answer: The browser gets HTTP 503 with the generic 'Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a few minutes.' login page, with the email kept and no cookie set. The user can retry.

q12.answer: Redis key TTL removes them: the 30-minute idle TTL, clamped to the 12-hour absolute deadline. There is no sweeper job.
